To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) service operational settings are beginning to view the role of performance from an organizational perspective; 2) performance measurement practices are still, to some extent, emphasizing financial performance measures; 3) the use of performance measures is not related to the organizational size; 4) there is a significant difference in the use of performance measurement between public and private service operational settings; and 5) service operational settings that use performance measures are more likely to be successful.
service operational managers use performance measures to monitor and improve the efficiency of service operations and to make strategic decisions.

the service organizations are beginning, to a certain degree, to view performance from an organizational perspective, and they are still, however, emphasizing financial measures in the performance measurement system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of performance measurement in service organizations and how it can be improved.

service organizations are in the early stages of implementing performance measurement systems.

service organizations are still, to some extent, emphasizing financial indicators of performance, but that they are beginning to view their performance from an overall, organizational perspective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
performance measurement systems are being used to support decision-making in service organizations.
the service organizations are beginning their journey towards a balanced scorecard approach to performance measurement.
the results of this research indicate that service organizations have begun to adopt a more comprehensive perspective of performance measures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
performance measures are important in the service sector and that service managers are becoming aware of the importance of using them in their organizations.
service organizations should not only focus on financial performance, but should also consider the use of nonfinancial performance measures.
